title: Constructing Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Tree with Conditional Generative Adversarial Network
problem: RSMT (Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Tree) construction for nets is NP-complete and computationally expensive; efficient algorithms are critical for physical design.
motivation: RSMT is fundamental backbone of global routers; current heuristics are computationally expensive; need for faster solutions.
method: The approach trains a conditional GAN (a machine learning system that transforms images) on pictures of optimally-wired nets. Each training image shows connection points paired with the shortest routing connecting them, teaching the GAN to recognize efficient wiring patterns. Once trained, the system generates new routings by presenting an unrouted net to the GAN, which outputs the predicted optimal wiring pattern.
key_novelty: The key idea is treating RSMT construction as an image-to-image translation problem, using conditional GANs instead of traditional routing algorithms.
contributions: Image-to-image translation formulation of RSMT problem
Wirelength error ≤ 0.348% on average vs optimal
Support for net degrees up to 50
First successful ML approach to RSMT
limitations: Abstract only; no runtime comparisons with traditional algorithms; no scalability analysis to full-chip routing; quality for nets larger than 50 pins unknown.
